clue.text: No working period; time for lunch?

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that is on is working
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A worker grumbles that there is no time off for the midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is an example: lunch is not always at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, the middle of the working day, is when people traditionally eat lunch.

clue.text: How mortgage may be secured free of charge

definitions.meaning: a mortgage loan is secured ..., literally ...
a drink ... is given free by the establishment

explanation.surface: A homebuyer wonders how a mortgage gets arranged at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: the loan is secured against the property. The second is the idiom for something paid for by the bar or shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a gift paid for by the business, while the literal phrase names a loan's security.

clue.text: Crazy about one girl

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for crazy wraps the letter for one

parts.note: mad means crazy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is madly keen on a particular girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old or poetic word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Spotted large number at church in past

indicators.note: in places the large number and the church between the two letters for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that a big crowd used to gather at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as 'seen', but it is the definition: marked with blotches.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotchy face or surface is covered in irregular patches, that is spotted.

clue.text: Miserly girls just avoided accidents

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or miserly
misses are girls or young women

explanation.surface: A pair of stingy girls narrowly escaped some mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR for mean with money is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Near misses are collisions or mishaps that were only narrowly avoided.

clue.text: Are they before or after chickens?

definitions.text: Are they before or after chickens?

parts.words: Are they before or after chickens?
parts.note: alludes to the old riddle of which came first, the chicken or the egg

explanation.surface: The old riddle about which came first, the chicken or what it hatched from.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens lay them and chicks hatch from them, the subject of the famous chicken-first puzzle.

clue.text: Starry artists tell a reviewer's hiding

indicators.note: the answer is hiding inside the run of words artists tell a reviewer

explanation.surface: Performers confide to a critic, who keeps something back; or a reviewer is giving them a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' signals the answer sitting inside artiSTS TELL A Reviewer; the surface tempts a thrashing reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means relating to the stars, so it is a synonym for starry.

clue.text: Impenetrable row of crops at one end of the country?

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop
a wall is a solid barrier, a row nothing gets through

explanation.surface: A dense line of cereal plants at the edge of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNWALL is the county at England's far south-western tip, hence one end of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county forms the extreme south-western extremity of Britain.

clue.text: Scores four? Many more

parts.note: a score is twenty, so four scores make a large total, many more than four

explanation.surface: A football fan asks whether a side netted four, and is told far more.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so four of them make the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Four twenties total this number, which is indeed many more than four.

clue.text: Work to do, then, promptly

indicators.note: work means rework or knead, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to get the chores done straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges TO DO THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving exactly at the appointed time is being punctual, i.e. prompt.

clue.text: Philosopher speaking in a crackly whisper

indicators.note: speaking means said out loud, so the philosopher's name is heard as a similar word

parts.note: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher lectures in a dry, crackling murmur.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertrand Russell (1872-1970) was a famous British philosopher; his surname is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is the soft crackling noise of leaves or paper, like a whisper.

clue.text: One's stocking up, ready for the occasional visitor to drop in

definitions.text: One's stocking up, ready for the occasional visitor to drop in

parts.words: One's stocking up, ready for the occasional visitor to drop in
parts.note: children hang up a stocking for the yearly visitor who comes down the chimney

explanation.surface: A host lays in supplies in case a guest drops by unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking up' reads as buying supplies but means a Christmas stocking hung up; the occasional visitor drops in down the chimney once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus is the yearly visitor who fills hung-up stockings after coming down the chimney.

clue.text: High-level plot for gore and mayhem

indicators.note: mayhem is chaos, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A storyline promising blood and chaos, like a slasher film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a story; it is a patch of ground. 'mayhem' rearranges FOR GORE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden on top of a building is a planted patch of ground high up.

clue.text: All the same, these letters give a basic education

definitions.text: All the same, these letters give a basic education

parts.words: All the same, these letters give a basic education
parts.note: reading, writing and arithmetic are each said to begin with the same letter

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, an alphabet lesson is the root of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the same' reads as 'nevertheless' but means the letters are identical: R, R and R, for reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading, writing and arithmetic are the core skills of elementary schooling.

clue.text: Boxed in, one has a trying time

definitions.text: Boxed in, one has a trying time

parts.words: Boxed in, one has a trying time
parts.note: a member of a jury sits in the jury box and helps try a case

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a confined space has a hard time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' means difficult on the surface, but here it is hearing a court case; the box is the jury box.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a jury sits in the box and spends the trial deciding a verdict.

clue.text: Request directions, being awry

parts.note: ask means request
E and W are the compass directions east and west

explanation.surface: A lost traveller asks the way and still goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something crooked or not straight, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Factory on holiday emptied and idle

parts.note: works is a factory, as in gasworks

indicators.note: emptied means all the inside letters are removed, leaving only the outer ones

explanation.surface: A factory shut for the holidays stands empty and still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps just H and Y of holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone work-shy avoids labour, i.e. lazy and idle.

clue.text: Grand group of swingers

parts.note: grand means large, a group is a band, and swing is the jazz style such large ensembles played

explanation.surface: A splendid crowd of party-goers, or of playground swings.
explanation.walkthrough: Swing was the jazz style of the large ensembles of the 1930s-40s, so the swingers are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jazz or dance orchestra of the swing era is known by this name.

clue.text: Pick one parent as the best

parts.note: opt means pick or choose
I is the Roman numeral one
mum is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A child has to choose which parent is better.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or best possible option.

clue.text: Not really expect to describe Bob's family quarrel?

definitions.meaning: to keep hoping when there is little chance
Bob Hope the comedian, so a quarrel in his family would be one Hope against another

explanation.surface: Someone doubts they could ever describe a feud in Bob's household.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Hope was an American comedian; '?' flags the whimsical second reading. 'to describe' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means clinging to hope despite little chance, i.e. not truly expecting success.

clue.text: Run after small girl, who may be on thin ice

definitions.text: who may be on thin ice

indicators.note: after places the run letter behind the small girl

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone chases a little girl who is taking a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on thin ice' suggests risk but here literally means gliding on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gliding on blades over a frozen pond may literally be on thin ice.

clue.text: Secured change of diet

indicators.note: a change of the word means its letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has fixed a new eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied is fastened with a knot, so made secure.

clue.text: Mountain originally broken in seven pieces

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
in pieces means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peak first shattered into seven fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives B; 'pieces' rearranges IN SEVEN into ENNEVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis in Scotland is Britain's highest mountain.

clue.text: Handle call

definitions.meaning: a handle is slang for a person's ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' reads as a verb but is the noun, slang for a name or nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for what a person is called, and to call is to give that label.

clue.text: Audibly breathe a cunning plan

definitions.meaning: to breathe with a whistling sound
British slang for a clever scheme

explanation.walkthrough: The scheme sense is British, schoolboyish slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is a whistling breath, and in British slang also a clever trick or scheme.

clue.text: Many distributed our menus

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A restaurant handed out plenty of its menus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges OUR MENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means great in number, so plentiful or many.
